ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals of square $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$, and point $O$ is also a vertex of square $A_1B_1C_1O$, with both squares having equal side lengths. No matter how square $A_1B_1C_1O$ is rotated around point $O$, the area of the overlapping part of the two squares is always equal to what fraction of the area of a square?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, construct OG$\perp$AB at G, and OH$\perp$BC at H. Assume AB intersects A$_{1}$O at point M.\\
Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle$OBH=$\angle$OBG=$45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral OGBH is a square,\\
$\therefore$OG=OH,\\
Since $\angle$GOM+$\angle$FOG=$\angle$FOH+$\angle$FOG=$90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle$GOM=$\angle$FOH,\\
$\therefore \triangle FOH \cong \triangle MOG$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore$Area of quadrilateral OFBM=Area of quadrilateral OGBH=$\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$ Area of square ABCD.

Thus the extra area and the missing area are equal, hence area(OMBF)=area(OGBH)=1/4 area(ABCD).

Draw OG perpendicular to AB and OH perpendicular to BC; these meet AB and BC at the midpoints G and H because O is the center of square ABCD. method.method_draft: Use a symmetry-sector argument. In the image, the overlap is the portion of ABCD lying inside the 90-degree angle formed at O by the two adjacent sides of the rotating square. Extend those two sides through O to full perpendicular lines. These two perpendicular lines divide square ABCD into four sectors. Because ABCD has 90-degree rotational symmetry about its center O, rotation by 90 degrees maps each sector to the next one, so the four sector areas are equal. The far two sides of square A1B1C1O do not cut the part inside ABCD: any point of ABCD is at distance at most half the diagonal of ABCD, which is less than the side length of either square, so once a point of ABCD lies in the angle from O, it is within the side-length bounds of the rotated square. Hence the overlap is exactly one of the four equal sectors of ABCD, giving area fraction 1/4.

推理：设正方形ABCD的边长为s，则正方形A1B1C1O的边长也为s。把旋转正方形从O出发的两条相邻边延长成过O的两条互相垂直的直线。这两条直线把正方形ABCD分成四个区域。因为O是正方形ABCD的中心，ABCD绕O旋转90°后与自身重合；同时这两条互相垂直的直线在90°旋转下也互相对应，所以这四个区域互相对应，面积相等。因此每个区域的面积都是正方形ABCD面积的1/4。
还需确认旋转正方形远离O的两条边不会截掉这个区域。对ABCD内任意点P，都有OP不超过正方形ABCD半条对角线，即OP≤s/√2<s。若P落在从O出发的那90°角内，则P沿旋转正方形两条边方向的坐标都非负，且都小于s，所以P一定在边长为s的旋转正方形内部。因此重叠部分恰好就是上述四个等面积区域中的一个。
最终答案：1/4。

推理：设正方形ABCD的边长为s，则正方形A1B1C1O的边长也为s。把旋转正方形从O出发的两条相邻边延长成过O的两条互相垂直的直线。这两条直线把正方形ABCD分成四个区域。因为O是正方形ABCD的中心，ABCD绕O旋转90°后与自身重合；同时这两条互相垂直的直线在90°旋转下也互相对应，所以这四个区域互相对应，面积相等。因此每个区域的面积都是正方形ABCD面积的1/4。
还需确认旋转正方形远离O的两条边不会截掉这个区域。对ABCD内任意点P，都有OP不超过正方形ABCD半条对角线，即OP≤s/√2<s。若P落在从O出发的那90°角内，则P沿旋转正方形两条边方向的坐标都非负，且都小于s，所以P一定在边长为s的旋转正方形内部。因此重叠部分恰好就是上述四个等面积区域中的一个。
最终答案：1/4。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This avoids constructing compensating triangles or using ASA congruence. It treats the rotated square as selecting one quadrant sector of the original square determined by two perpendicular lines through the center, then uses rotational symmetry to get equal areas.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the image that the rotating square contributes a right angle at O and that the shaded overlap is the portion of ABCD inside that right-angle sector, with the other sides of the rotating square outside the shown original square region.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the statement that ABCD is a square with diagonals intersecting at O, that A1B1C1O is a congruent square with vertex O, and that it may be rotated arbitrarily around O.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use 90-degree rotational symmetry of a square about its center, the fact that two perpendicular lines through the center form four sectors cyclically mapped by that rotation, and the distance bound that points of ABCD lie within radius side/sqrt(2) from O, less than the square side length.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the diagonals of square $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$, and point $O$ is also a vertex of square $A_1B_1C_1O$, with both squares having equal side lengths. No matter how square $A_1B_1C_1O$ is rotated around point $O$, the area of the overlapping part of the two squares is always equal to what fraction of the area of a square?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, construct OG$\perp$AB at G, and OH$\perp$BC at H. Assume AB intersects A$_1$O at point M.\\
Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle$OBH=$\angle$OBG=$45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral OGBH is a square,\\
$\therefore$OG=OH,\\
Since $\angle$GOM+$\angle$FOG=$\angle$FOH+$\angle$FOG=$90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle$GOM=$\angle$FOH,\\
$\therefore \triangle FOH \cong \triangle MOG$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore$Area of quadrilateral OFBM=Area of quadrilateral OGBH=$\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$ Area of square ABCD.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right, and the two diagonals intersect at the center point O. There is also a rotated square A1B1C1O with side length equal to that of ABCD, taking O as one vertex. The shaded part in the figure is the overlapping region of the two squares, and its boundary can be regarded as quadrilateral OMBF, where OA1 intersects AB at M, and OC1 intersects BC at F.

Reasoning: Draw OG⊥AB through O, meeting at G, and draw OH⊥BC, meeting at H. Because O is the center of square ABCD, G and H are respectively the midpoints of AB and BC, and quadrilateral OGBH is a one-fourth small square of ABCD, therefore area(OGBH)=1/4 area(ABCD).

Compare the overlapping quadrilateral OMBF with the small square OGBH: compared with OGBH, OMBF has the extra triangle MOG, and at the same time lacks triangle FOH. Since OA1⊥OC1, OM⊥OF; also OG⊥OH, therefore ∠GOM+∠FOG=90°, and ∠FOH+∠FOG=90°, so ∠GOM=∠FOH. Also because OG=OH, and ∠OGM=∠FHO=90°, △MOG≅△FOH. Thus the extra area and the missing area are equal, hence area(OMBF)=area(OGBH)=1/4 area(ABCD).
